sentences.text:
This application under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (CrPC) is filed seeking quash of FIR in Crime No. I-106 of 2017, registered with Sarkhej Police Station, Ahmedabad for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 294B and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC)
and Sections 3 and 7 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
2.

Heard the learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/20651/2017 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined for the second respondent, who is the de facto complainant and the learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent - State.

sentences.text: 3. When the matter is taken up for hearing, the learned counsel for the applicants as well as the learned counsel for the second respondent - de facto complainant would submit that both the parties have entered into compromise and they have settled all the disputes between them and they have decided to compound the offence.
The learned counsel for the applicants has also filed the affidavit of the second respondent - de facto complainant to this effect.
4. The de facto complainant is physically present before the Court today.

When questioned, she has unequivocally stated that she has entered into compromise with the accused and they have amicably settled the dispute and that, she has no objection to quash the FIR that is registered against the applicants, who are the accused Nos. 2 and 3 respectively.

5. Although, the offences for which the FIR was registered are of non-compoundable offences, as per the dictum laid down by the Apex Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303, in appropriate cases, where the offences have not impact on the society, the Court, in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (CrPC), can permit the parties to compound the offences even which are non- NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/20651/2017 ORDER DATED: 13/02/2024 undefined compoundable.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, some cases are exempted which are catelogued in the said judgment of the Apex Court, the present case is not falling within the said exempted cases.
6. Therefore, permission is accorded to the applicant and the de facto complainant to compound the offence as prayed for and the compromise is recorded.

The FIR in Crime No. I-106 of 2017, registered with Sarkhej Police Station, Ahmedabad for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 294B and 114 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 7 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, is hereby quashed against the applicants, who are accused Nos. 2 and 3 respectively.
